title: Squad Formation Tactics
description: The user commands a tactical squad of one Soldier and one Xbot on a grid battlefield. They must assign movement waypoints, toggle combat stances, allocate a shared energy pool between the two units, and execute or undo formation plans before committing a final battle sequence. Energy is conserved: boosting one unit's shield drains the other's attack power.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a tactical squad formation game on a 10x10 grid floor. Load soldier.glb and Xbot.glb using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Place the Soldier at grid cell (2,2) and the Xbot at (7,7). Use a perspective camera at position (5,12,14) looking at the grid center. Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light from (5,10,5) casting shadows onto a ground plane.

Interaction requirements (10-14 steps, L6 difficulty):
1. Click a unit to select it (highlight with an emissive outline or color tint). A HUD panel shows the selected unit's stats.
2. Right-click a grid cell to assign a movement waypoint for the selected unit. Show a path line from unit to waypoint. Units play their walk animation when moving.
3. Implement a shared Energy Pool of 100 points displayed as a bar. The user drags a slider to allocate energy between Soldier (Attack) and Xbot (Shield). Conservation law: Attack + Shield always equals 100. Changing one automatically adjusts the other.
4. Each unit has a stance toggle button (Aggressive / Defensive) that changes their idle animation clip and tints their model red or blue respectively.
5. Add an Execute button that moves both units simultaneously along their waypoints with walk animations.
6. Implement full Undo/Redo stack (at least 5 levels) for all actions: waypoint assignments, energy allocation changes, and stance toggles. Bind to Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y and also provide on-screen buttons.
7. After both units reach waypoints, play an attack or defend animation clip based on their stance.
8. Display a turn counter and a log panel listing all actions taken.
9. Add a Reset Turn button that reverts all changes for the current turn using the undo stack.
10. Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation. Render grid lines and cell highlights on hover. All UI overlays use HTML/CSS positioned absolutely over the canvas.
